intro: Welcome back! You can already tell a story out loud. Now you'll write one: a story of about 100 words with a title, a strong first line and clear paragraphs, and then a short article or review that gives your opinion and a recommendation. Warm-up: think of a place you love in your city, or a day that went completely wrong.
teachingNotes: This writing lesson builds on b1-telling-stories (the shape scene → events → ending and feelings; past continuous for the background, past simple for the events, past perfect to go back; suddenly, finally, in the end; Luckily / Unfortunately; -ing vs -ed feelings) and b1-linkers-contrast-purpose (although / even though + subject + verb, However, at the start of a new sentence, because vs because of / due to, to / so that for purpose). Recap each in one line, don't re-teach them. The topic-sentence part links to the main idea from b1-reading-articles and to 'kalimat utama' and 'paragraf deduktif' that learners know from Bahasa Indonesia at school.

A story of about 100 words (80–120, counted between spaces; the title doesn't count): 1) a short title, 2) a first line that hooks the reader (a surprise, a problem, a strong feeling: 'I only wanted to go home, but it took me five hours.'), 3) the scene in one or two sentences, 4) the events in order in the past simple, with suddenly / then / after that and had + third form to go back, 5) a clear ending with a feeling. Usually three short paragraphs: scene, events, ending. Common errors: the Indonesian no-tense trap in the second and third verbs (*'I got off and I order an ojek'); every verb in -ing; starting with a long greeting or self-introduction (*'Hello everyone, my name is Budi and I want to tell you a story about…') as in a speech at school; ending with 'The end.' or a moral lesson instead of what happened and how you felt.

The 'dan … dan …' habit: Indonesian writing often joins many ideas in one very long sentence with dan, lalu, kemudian, sehingga. In English this is hard to read: *'We went to the beach and it was raining and we stayed in the car and we ate our lunch there.' Teach the fix: one idea or two per sentence (about 8–20 words), and a linker that says HOW the ideas connect: then / after that (order), suddenly (surprise), but / However, / although (contrast), because / so (reason / result), to / so that (purpose). Keep the rule from the linkers lesson: one linker per sentence (*'Although it was late, but…'), and However starts a new sentence with a comma after it.

Topic sentences and paragraphs: each paragraph has ONE main idea, and in English articles and reviews the first sentence usually says it (the topic sentence); the other sentences support it with examples, reasons, numbers and details. A new main idea = a new paragraph (leave an empty line between paragraphs online). A good topic sentence is not too narrow (a single detail: 'The coffee costs Rp28,000.') and not too broad ('Bandung is a city in Indonesia.'). Common errors: one long block of text with no paragraphs; starting a paragraph with a detail; a sentence that doesn't belong to the paragraph's idea.

Short articles and reviews (80–120 words): a title; an opening question or a surprising fact to catch the reader ('Where can you drink good coffee next to rice fields?'); 2–3 paragraphs, each with a topic sentence; an opinion with reasons (In my opinion, … because …; I think …); the good and the bad (However, … / Although …); a recommendation at the end: I'd recommend + a noun or -ing (I'd recommend the soto / going on a weekday), It's worth + -ing (It's worth visiting), If you like …, you'll love … (first conditional, A2), You should try …. Treat I'd recommend and It's worth + -ing as phrases to remember. Common errors: *'I recommend you to try …' (→ I'd recommend + -ing … / You should try …), *'It's worth to visit' (→ It's worth visiting), *'In my opinion, I think …' (choose one), *'This place is very recommended' (from 'sangat direkomendasikan' → I'd really recommend this place).

Limits: no passive, relative clauses (who / which / that / where), second conditional, reported speech, used to or present perfect continuous in examples; tell what people said with direct speech if needed. British vs American: favourite / favorite, centre / center, at the weekend / on the weekend. For the free writing (the 100-word story and the review), praise the shape first, then correct one or two things only, usually a verb left in the present or a very long 'and … and …' sentence. Typed answers are lowercased when checked, so give feedback on capitals, titles and paragraphs in the free writing, not in the checkpoint.

keyPoints.title: A story of about 100 words
keyPoints.explanation: Give your story a short title and a first line that makes people want to read on (a surprise, a problem, a strong feeling), not a long greeting. Then three short paragraphs: the scene (was/were + -ing), the events in order (past simple, with had + third form to go back), and a clear ending with how you felt. Check every verb: in a past story, they all change.

examples.en: I only wanted to go home, but it took me five hours.
examples.id: Aku cuma ingin pulang, tapi butuh lima jam.

examples.en: Twenty minutes later, I realised I had taken the wrong bus!
examples.id: Dua puluh menit kemudian, aku sadar aku salah naik bus!

examples.en: I was wet and exhausted, but I couldn't stop laughing.
examples.id: Aku basah dan capek sekali, tapi aku tidak bisa berhenti tertawa.

id.title: Cerita sekitar 100 kata
id.explanation: Beri ceritamu judul pendek dan kalimat pertama yang membuat orang ingin terus membaca (kejutan, masalah, perasaan yang kuat), bukan salam yang panjang. Lalu tiga paragraf pendek: latar (was/were + -ing), kejadian-kejadiannya berurutan (past simple, dengan had + bentuk ketiga untuk kembali ke masa sebelumnya), dan akhir yang jelas dengan apa yang kamu rasakan. Periksa setiap kata kerja: dalam cerita lampau, semuanya berubah.

keyPoints.title: A short article or review
keyPoints.explanation: Start with a title and an opening question or a surprising fact. Write 2–3 paragraphs: what it is, the good and the bad (However, … / Although …), and your opinion with reasons. End with a recommendation: I'd recommend + a noun or -ing, It's worth + -ing, If you like …, you'll love …. Not 'I recommend you to try' or 'It's worth to visit'.

examples.en: Where can you drink good coffee next to green rice fields?
examples.id: Di mana kamu bisa minum kopi enak di sebelah sawah hijau?

examples.en: I'd recommend going on a weekday, and it's worth visiting just for the view.
examples.id: Aku sarankan datang di hari kerja, dan tempat ini layak dikunjungi walaupun hanya untuk pemandangannya.

id.title: Artikel atau review pendek
id.explanation: Mulai dengan judul dan pertanyaan pembuka atau fakta yang mengejutkan. Tulis 2–3 paragraf: tempat atau barangnya apa, sisi baik dan buruknya (However, … / Although …), dan pendapatmu dengan alasannya. Tutup dengan rekomendasi: I'd recommend + kata benda atau -ing, It's worth + -ing, If you like …, you'll love …. Bukan 'I recommend you to try' atau 'It's worth to visit'.

keyPoints.title: One paragraph, one main idea
keyPoints.explanation: Each paragraph has one main idea. Say it in the first sentence: the topic sentence (kalimat utama). The other sentences support it with examples, reasons and details. A new idea needs a new paragraph. Write shorter sentences joined with clear linkers, not one long sentence with 'and … and … and …'.

examples.en: The view is the best thing about this café.
examples.id: Pemandangannya adalah hal terbaik dari kafe ini.

examples.en: All the tables are outside, next to the rice fields.
examples.id: Semua mejanya di luar, di sebelah sawah.

examples.en: We drove to the beach. However, it was raining, so we stayed in the car.
examples.id: Kami menyetir ke pantai. Namun, hujan turun, jadi kami tetap di mobil.

id.title: Satu paragraf, satu ide pokok
id.explanation: Setiap paragraf punya satu ide pokok. Tulis ide itu di kalimat pertama: topic sentence (kalimat utama). Kalimat-kalimat lainnya mendukungnya dengan contoh, alasan dan detail. Ide baru butuh paragraf baru. Tulis kalimat yang lebih pendek dengan kata penghubung yang jelas, bukan satu kalimat panjang dengan 'and … and … and …'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the verbs in this line from a story: Last month I visit Yogyakarta and I see the sunrise at Borobudur.
expected: last month i visited yogyakarta and i saw the sunrise at borobudur
last month i visited yogyakarta and saw the sunrise at borobudur
i visited yogyakarta last month and i saw the sunrise at borobudur
i visited yogyakarta last month and saw the sunrise at borobudur
guidedPractice.hint: It's a past story, so both verbs change: visit → visited, see → saw.

guidedPractice.prompt: This sentence is too long. Make two sentences, and start the second one with Suddenly: We were having dinner at a warung and the lights went out and everyone screamed.
expected: we were having dinner at a warung suddenly the lights went out and everyone screamed
we were having dinner at a warung suddenly the lights went out everyone screamed
guidedPractice.hint: Sentence 1 = the scene (were having). Sentence 2 = the surprise: Suddenly the lights went out…

guidedPractice.prompt: Which sentence is the topic sentence of this paragraph? Write A, B or C. A: The rent is only Rp1,500,000 a month. B: My new kos is perfect for me. C: It's a five-minute walk from my office.
expected: b
sentence b
guidedPractice.hint: Which sentence gives the main idea? The other two are reasons for it.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete the recommendation with the right form of 'book': The restaurant is always full on Saturday night, so I'd recommend ___ a table.
expected: booking

independentPractice.prompt: Write a story of about 100 words (80–120) called 'A Day I Won't Forget'. Checklist: a first line that hooks the reader; the scene with was/were + -ing; the events in the past simple, with Suddenly and one had + third form; a clear ending with how you felt; three short paragraphs; no long greeting at the start.
expected: i only wanted to buy some medicine but it took me all evening it was a friday night in bandung and it was raining i was walking to the pharmacy near my kos suddenly i realised i had left my wallet at home i ran back but my kos was locked in the end my neighbour opened the door and i got my medicine at ten oclock i was tired and wet but i felt so proud of myself
independentPractice.hint: Check: title, hook, scene (was/were + -ing), events (past simple + Suddenly + had …), ending + feeling, three paragraphs, 80–120 words, every verb in the past.

independentPractice.prompt: Write a short review (80–120 words) of a café, warung or place in your city. Checklist: a title; an opening question or a surprising fact; 2–3 paragraphs, each with a topic sentence; the good and the bad with However or although; your opinion with a reason; a recommendation at the end (I'd recommend … / It's worth …).
expected: i would recommend
id recommend
its worth
it is worth
independentPractice.hint: Title → opening question → the good → the bad (However, …) → In my opinion, … because … → I'd recommend … / It's worth + -ing.

independentPractice.prompt: Write a topic sentence for a paragraph with these details: no traffic, more time with your family, lunch in your own kitchen. The paragraph is about working from home.
expected: working from home has many good points
working from home has a lot of advantages
working from home has many advantages
there are many good things about working from home
working from home is great
i love working from home
independentPractice.hint: Say the one main idea that all three details support, in one sentence.

assessment.prompt: Complete the story with the right form of 'wait': It was a hot Saturday afternoon in Surabaya. Hundreds of football fans ___ outside the stadium when the gates suddenly opened.
assessment.rubric: Correct: were waiting (the scene, already in progress when the gates opened). 'was waiting' = 60 (right tense, but fans = they → were). 'waited' or 'had waited' = 30 (past, but not the background). 'wait' or 'are waiting' = 0 (the no-tense trap).

assessment.prompt: Complete with although, however or because of: It was Saturday night at a popular seafood restaurant in Makassar. ___ we arrived early, all the tables were full, so we ate at a small warung next door.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Although (a surprise: we were early, but the tables were full; a subject + verb follows). Also accept 'Even though'. 'However' = 0 (it starts a new sentence and can't join two parts). 'Because of' = 0 (it needs a noun and gives a reason, not a surprise).

assessment.prompt: These three sentences make one paragraph of an article. Which one is the topic sentence? Write A, B or C. A: On Jalan Sudirman, there is now a special lane for bikes. B: More and more office workers in Jakarta are cycling to work. C: Some offices also have showers and bike parking for their staff.
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (the main idea; A and C are details that support it). A or C = 0 (a single detail, too narrow to be the main idea).

assessment.prompt: Read the paragraph. One sentence doesn't belong, because it doesn't support the topic sentence. Write its number. '(1) Bandung is a great place for a weekend trip from Jakarta. (2) It isn't far: you can get there by train or by car. (3) The weather is cooler, and there are lots of cafés and parks. (4) My cousin is studying medicine in Surabaya. (5) You can also buy cheap clothes at the factory outlets.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: 4 (it's about Surabaya and a cousin, not about a weekend trip to Bandung). 1 = 0 (that's the topic sentence). 2, 3 or 5 = 0 (they are reasons for the main idea).

assessment.prompt: Complete the last line of a review with the right form of 'see': The new photo exhibition at the National Museum is small, but the old photos of Jakarta are amazing, and tickets are only Rp15,000. It's really worth ___ .
assessment.rubric: Correct: seeing (It's worth + -ing). 'to see' = 20 (a common mistake: worth is not followed by to). 'see' or 'saw' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake in the last line of this food review: I recommend you to try the soto ayam.
acceptableAnswers: id recommend trying the soto ayam
i would recommend trying the soto ayam
i recommend trying the soto ayam
i would recommend the soto ayam
i recommend that you try the soto ayam
id recommend that you try the soto ayam
i would recommend that you try the soto ayam
i recommend you try the soto ayam
id recommend you try the soto ayam
you should try the soto ayam
you should really try the soto ayam
id really recommend the soto ayam
id really recommend trying the soto ayam
i really recommend the soto ayam
i really recommend trying the soto ayam
assessment.rubric: Correct: recommend + -ing or + a noun (I'd recommend trying the soto ayam / I'd recommend the soto ayam), I recommend (that) you try …, or You should try the soto ayam. 'I recommend you trying …' = 40. Keeping 'recommend you to try' = 0 (recommend is not followed by someone + to).

blocks.text:
In the last lesson you **told** a story. Writing one uses the same shape (scene → events → ending and feelings), with a few extras:
- **A title**: short, and it makes people curious: *The Longest Trip Home*.
- **A first line that hooks the reader** (*hook* = kail: it 'catches' the reader). Start with a surprise, a problem or a strong feeling: *I only wanted to go home, but it took me five hours.*
- **Three short paragraphs**: 1) the scene, 2) the events, 3) the ending and how you felt.
- **About 100 words**: between 80 and 120. Count the words between spaces (*I'm* = one word). The title doesn't count.

Here's a story of 106 words. Look at what each part does.

id.text:
Di pelajaran sebelumnya kamu **menceritakan** cerita secara lisan. Menulis cerita memakai bentuk yang sama (latar → kejadian → akhir dan perasaan), dengan beberapa tambahan:
- **Judul**: pendek, dan membuat orang penasaran: *The Longest Trip Home* (Perjalanan Pulang Terpanjang).
- **Kalimat pertama yang 'mengait' pembaca** (*hook* = kail: kalimat ini 'menangkap' pembaca). Mulai dengan kejutan, masalah atau perasaan yang kuat: *I only wanted to go home, but it took me five hours.*
- **Tiga paragraf pendek**: 1) latar, 2) kejadian-kejadiannya, 3) akhir dan apa yang kamu rasakan.
- **Sekitar 100 kata**: antara 80 dan 120. Hitung kata yang dipisahkan spasi (*I'm* = satu kata). Judul tidak dihitung.

Ini cerita 106 kata. Perhatikan tugas setiap bagiannya.

rows.en: The Longest Trip Home
rows.id: Perjalanan Pulang Terpanjang

rows.en: I only wanted to go home, but it took me five hours.
rows.id: Aku cuma ingin pulang, tapi butuh lima jam.
rows.note: the hook: a problem that makes you curious

id.note: kalimat pengait: masalah yang membuat penasaran

rows.en: It was a Friday evening in Jakarta, and it was raining heavily. I was standing at the bus stop with hundreds of other tired workers.
rows.id: Waktu itu Jumat sore di Jakarta, dan hujan deras. Aku sedang berdiri di halte bersama ratusan pekerja lain yang capek.

rows.en: After an hour, a bus finally came, and I got on. Twenty minutes later, I realised I had taken the wrong bus! I got off and tried to order an ojek. Unfortunately, my phone had died.
rows.id: Setelah satu jam, akhirnya bus datang, dan aku naik. Dua puluh menit kemudian, aku sadar aku salah naik bus! Aku turun dan mencoba memesan ojek. Sayangnya, HP-ku sudah mati.
rows.note: paragraph 2, the events: past simple; had + third form goes back

id.note: paragraf 2, kejadian: past simple; had + bentuk ketiga untuk kembali ke masa sebelumnya

rows.en: In the end, a kind woman at a warung let me use her phone, and I got home at midnight. I was wet and exhausted, but I couldn't stop laughing. What a night!
rows.id: Akhirnya, seorang ibu yang baik di warung meminjamkan HP-nya, dan aku sampai di rumah tengah malam. Aku basah dan capek sekali, tapi aku tidak bisa berhenti tertawa. Malam yang luar biasa!
rows.note: paragraph 3, the ending and a feeling

blocks.text:
**Don't start with a long greeting.** At school we often learn to start like a speech: *Hello everyone, my name is Budi, and today I want to tell you a story about my holiday.* ✗ In a written story, that wastes your best line. Go straight to the hook. And don't finish with *The end.* or a lesson (*So we must always be careful.*): finish with what happened and how you felt.
*realised* is British spelling; Americans write *realized*.

id.text:
**Jangan mulai dengan salam yang panjang.** Di sekolah kita sering belajar membuka seperti pidato: *Hello everyone, my name is Budi, and today I want to tell you a story about my holiday.* ✗ Dalam cerita tertulis, itu membuang kalimat terbaikmu. Langsung ke kalimat pengait. Dan jangan tutup dengan *The end.* atau pesan moral (*So we must always be careful.*): tutup dengan apa yang terjadi dan apa yang kamu rasakan.
*realised* adalah ejaan British; orang Amerika menulis *realized*.

blocks.prompt: Which is the best last line for a story about a bad day at the office?
options: The end. Thank you for reading my story.
In the end, my boss laughed too, and I went home tired but happy.
So, we must always check our emails before a meeting.
blocks.explain: A good ending says how the story ended and how you felt: In the end, … tired but happy. 'The end. Thank you for reading' and a moral lesson don't finish the story itself.

id.prompt: Mana kalimat terakhir yang paling bagus untuk cerita tentang hari yang buruk di kantor?
id.explain: Akhir yang bagus menceritakan bagaimana ceritanya berakhir dan apa yang kamu rasakan: In the end, … tired but happy. 'The end. Thank you for reading' dan pesan moral tidak menutup ceritanya sendiri.

blocks.text:
In Indonesian we often write one very long sentence with *dan … lalu … dan … sehingga …*. In English, a sentence like this is hard to read:
*We went to the beach and it was raining and we stayed in the car and we ate our lunch there and we went home.* ✗
The fix: **one or two ideas per sentence** (about 8–20 words), and a **linker** (kata penghubung) that says **how** the ideas connect:
- order: **then, after that, finally**
- a surprise: **suddenly**
- contrast: **but, However, (new sentence), although**
- reason and result: **because, because of, so**
- purpose: **to, so that**

And from the last lesson: in a past story, **every verb** is in a past form, also the second and third verb after *and*.

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering menulis satu kalimat yang sangat panjang dengan *dan … lalu … dan … sehingga …*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, kalimat seperti ini sulit dibaca:
*We went to the beach and it was raining and we stayed in the car and we ate our lunch there and we went home.* ✗
Perbaikannya: **satu atau dua ide per kalimat** (sekitar 8–20 kata), dan **linker** (kata penghubung) yang menunjukkan **bagaimana** ide-idenya berhubungan:
- urutan: **then, after that, finally**
- kejutan: **suddenly**
- pertentangan: **but, However, (kalimat baru), although**
- alasan dan akibat: **because, because of, so**
- tujuan: **to, so that**

Dan dari pelajaran sebelumnya: dalam cerita lampau, **setiap kata kerja** memakai bentuk lampau, termasuk kata kerja kedua dan ketiga setelah *and*.

rows.en: We drove to the beach. However, it was raining, so we stayed in the car.
rows.id: Kami menyetir ke pantai. Namun, hujan turun, jadi kami tetap di mobil.
rows.note: However starts a new sentence; so = the result

id.note: However memulai kalimat baru; so = akibatnya

rows.en: We ate our lunch there. After that, we went home.
rows.id: Kami makan siang di sana. Setelah itu, kami pulang.

rows.en: Although we were tired, we stayed until the end of the concert.
rows.id: Meskipun kami capek, kami tetap di sana sampai konsernya selesai.
rows.note: although + subject + verb: no 'but' after it

id.note: although + subjek + kata kerja: tanpa 'but' setelahnya

rows.en: I left the office early so that I could catch the last train.
rows.id: Aku pulang kantor lebih awal supaya bisa naik kereta terakhir.

rows.en: I got off the bus and ordered an ojek.
rows.id: Aku turun dari bus dan memesan ojek.
rows.note: both verbs in the past (not 'and I order')

id.note: kedua kata kerja dalam bentuk lampau (bukan 'and I order')

blocks.text:
**One linker per sentence.** *Although it was late, but we went out.* ✗ (from *Meskipun …, tetapi …*) → *Although it was late, we went out.* ✓ or *It was late, but we went out.* ✓
**However** can't join two parts like *but*: *The hotel was cheap, however it was clean.* ✗ → *The hotel was cheap. **However,** it was clean.* ✓
A short sentence is not a 'baby' sentence: good English writers mix short and medium sentences.

id.text:
**Satu linker per kalimat.** *Although it was late, but we went out.* ✗ (dari *Meskipun …, tetapi …*) → *Although it was late, we went out.* ✓ atau *It was late, but we went out.* ✓
**However** tidak bisa menyambung dua bagian seperti *but*: *The hotel was cheap, however it was clean.* ✗ → *The hotel was cheap. **However,** it was clean.* ✓
Kalimat pendek bukan kalimat 'anak kecil': penulis bahasa Inggris yang bagus mencampur kalimat pendek dan sedang.

blocks.prompt: Which version is the best writing?
options: We missed the train and we waited for two hours and we got home late and we were hungry.
We missed the train, so we waited for two hours. We got home late and very hungry.
Although we missed the train, but we waited for two hours and we got home late and hungry.
blocks.explain: Two clear sentences, and so shows the result. The first version is one long 'and … and … and' sentence. The third uses although and but together, and the although doesn't fit: missing the train and waiting aren't a surprise.

id.prompt: Versi mana yang tulisannya paling bagus?
id.explain: Dua kalimat yang jelas, dan so menunjukkan akibatnya. Versi pertama adalah satu kalimat panjang 'and … and … and'. Versi ketiga memakai although dan but bersamaan, dan although-nya tidak cocok: ketinggalan kereta lalu menunggu bukan hal yang mengejutkan.

id.title: Kalimat pendek, kata penghubung yang jelas

blocks.text:
A **paragraph** is a group of sentences about **one main idea**. In English articles and reviews, the **first sentence** usually says that idea: it's the **topic sentence**. You know this from Bahasa Indonesia at school: *kalimat utama* at the start = *paragraf deduktif*. (In the reading lesson, you looked for the main idea. Now you write it.)
The other sentences **support** it: examples, reasons, numbers, details.
A good topic sentence is:
- **not too narrow**: one detail (*A cup costs Rp28,000.*) can't hold a whole paragraph;
- **not too broad**: *Bandung is a city in Indonesia.* says nothing new.

**A new main idea = a new paragraph.** Online and in emails, leave an empty line between paragraphs. Most short paragraphs have 2–5 sentences.

id.text:
**Paragraf** adalah sekelompok kalimat tentang **satu ide pokok**. Dalam artikel dan review berbahasa Inggris, **kalimat pertama** biasanya menyatakan ide itu: itulah **topic sentence**. Kamu sudah tahu ini dari pelajaran Bahasa Indonesia di sekolah: *kalimat utama* di awal = *paragraf deduktif*. (Di pelajaran membaca, kamu mencari ide pokok. Sekarang kamu yang menulisnya.)
Kalimat-kalimat lainnya **mendukung** ide itu: contoh, alasan, angka, detail (*kalimat penjelas*).
Topic sentence yang bagus itu:
- **tidak terlalu sempit**: satu detail (*A cup costs Rp28,000.*) tidak bisa menampung satu paragraf;
- **tidak terlalu luas**: *Bandung is a city in Indonesia.* tidak memberi info baru.

**Ide pokok baru = paragraf baru.** Di internet dan email, beri satu baris kosong di antara paragraf. Kebanyakan paragraf pendek terdiri dari 2–5 kalimat.

rows.en: The view is the best thing about this café.
rows.id: Pemandangannya adalah hal terbaik dari kafe ini.

rows.en: All the tables are outside, next to the rice fields.
rows.id: Semua mejanya di luar, di sebelah sawah.

rows.en: On a clear morning you can see the mountains.
rows.id: Kalau pagi cerah, kamu bisa melihat pegunungan.

rows.en: However, the café isn't perfect.
rows.id: Namun, kafenya tidak sempurna.
rows.note: a new idea → a new paragraph and a new topic sentence

id.note: ide baru → paragraf baru dan topic sentence baru

rows.en: At the weekend it's very crowded, and the road to it is narrow and busy.
rows.id: Saat akhir pekan kafenya sangat ramai, dan jalan ke sana sempit dan padat.

blocks.text:
**Every sentence must support the topic sentence.** If a sentence is about something else (in a paragraph about the café's view: *My cousin works in a bank.*), take it out or move it to another paragraph. And don't write one big block of text: the reader needs the breaks to follow you.
*at the weekend* is British; Americans say *on the weekend*.

id.text:
**Setiap kalimat harus mendukung topic sentence.** Kalau sebuah kalimat membahas hal lain (di paragraf tentang pemandangan kafe: *My cousin works in a bank.*), buang atau pindahkan ke paragraf lain. Dan jangan menulis satu blok teks besar: pembaca butuh jeda untuk mengikuti tulisanmu.
*at the weekend* adalah bahasa Inggris British; orang Amerika bilang *on the weekend*.

blocks.prompt: This text needs two paragraphs. Which sentence should start the second paragraph? (1) Our new office in Kuningan is great. (2) It's only five minutes from the MRT station. (3) The rooms are bright, and there's a small garden on the roof. (4) However, the area around it has some problems. (5) Lunch is expensive, and the traffic is terrible after 5 p.m.
blocks.explain: Sentences 1–3 are about the good office. Sentence 4 starts a new main idea (the problems around it), so it's the topic sentence of paragraph 2. Sentence 5 supports it.

id.prompt: Teks ini perlu dua paragraf. Kalimat mana yang harus memulai paragraf kedua? (1) Our new office in Kuningan is great. (2) It's only five minutes from the MRT station. (3) The rooms are bright, and there's a small garden on the roof. (4) However, the area around it has some problems. (5) Lunch is expensive, and the traffic is terrible after 5 p.m.
id.explain: Kalimat 1–3 membahas kantor yang bagus. Kalimat 4 memulai ide pokok baru (masalah di sekitarnya), jadi itu topic sentence paragraf 2. Kalimat 5 mendukungnya.

blocks.text:
A **review** gives your opinion of a place, a film, a product or an app. A short **article** (for a blog, a company newsletter, a campus magazine) gives information and ideas about a topic. Both have the same shape:
- **A title**, often with the main idea: *Kopi Sawah: coffee with a view*.
- **An opening question or a surprising fact**: *Where can you drink good coffee next to green rice fields?*
- **2–3 paragraphs**, each with a topic sentence: what it is, the good, the bad.
- **Your opinion with reasons**: *In my opinion, … because …* / *I think …*
- **A recommendation** at the end: *I'd recommend* + a noun or -ing (*I'd recommend the soto / going early*), *It's worth* + -ing (*It's worth visiting*), *If you like …, you'll love …*, *You should try …*.

*I'd recommend* (= I would recommend) and *It's worth + -ing* are **phrases to remember**: just learn them as they are.

id.text:
**Review** memberi pendapatmu tentang sebuah tempat, film, produk atau aplikasi. **Artikel** pendek (untuk blog, buletin kantor, majalah kampus) memberi informasi dan ide tentang suatu topik. Keduanya punya bentuk yang sama:
- **Judul**, sering berisi ide pokoknya: *Kopi Sawah: coffee with a view*.
- **Pertanyaan pembuka atau fakta yang mengejutkan**: *Where can you drink good coffee next to green rice fields?*
- **2–3 paragraf**, masing-masing dengan topic sentence: apa tempatnya, sisi baiknya, sisi buruknya.
- **Pendapatmu dengan alasan**: *In my opinion, … because …* / *I think …*
- **Rekomendasi** di akhir: *I'd recommend* + kata benda atau -ing (*I'd recommend the soto / going early*), *It's worth* + -ing (*It's worth visiting* = layak dikunjungi), *If you like …, you'll love …*, *You should try …*.

*I'd recommend* (= I would recommend, aku sarankan) dan *It's worth + -ing* adalah **frasa untuk diingat**: hafalkan saja bentuknya.

rows.en: Kopi Sawah: coffee with a view

rows.en: Where can you drink good coffee next to green rice fields, only 30 minutes from Bandung? Try Kopi Sawah in Lembang.
rows.id: Di mana kamu bisa minum kopi enak di sebelah sawah hijau, hanya 30 menit dari Bandung? Coba Kopi Sawah di Lembang.

rows.en: The view is the best thing about this café. All the tables are outside, next to the rice fields, and on a clear morning you can see the mountains. The coffee is good too, and a cup costs about Rp28,000.
rows.id: Pemandangannya adalah hal terbaik dari kafe ini. Semua mejanya di luar, di sebelah sawah, dan kalau pagi cerah kamu bisa melihat pegunungan. Kopinya juga enak, dan secangkir harganya sekitar Rp28.000.

rows.en: However, the café isn't perfect. At the weekend it's very crowded, and the road to it is narrow and busy. The food menu is small, although the pisang goreng is delicious.
rows.id: Namun, kafenya tidak sempurna. Saat akhir pekan sangat ramai, dan jalan ke sana sempit dan padat. Menu makanannya sedikit, walaupun pisang gorengnya enak sekali.

rows.en: In my opinion, it's the perfect place for a slow morning. I'd recommend going on a weekday, and it's worth visiting just for the view.
rows.id: Menurutku, ini tempat yang sempurna untuk pagi yang santai. Aku sarankan datang di hari kerja, dan tempat ini layak dikunjungi walaupun hanya untuk pemandangannya.

blocks.text:
**Recommendation traps:**
- *I recommend you to visit the night market.* ✗ → *I'd recommend **visiting** the night market.* / *I'd recommend **the night market**.* / *You **should visit** the night market.* ✓
- *It's worth **to visit**.* ✗ → *It's worth **visiting**.* ✓ (worth + -ing)
- *This place is very recommended.* ✗ (from *sangat direkomendasikan*) → *I'd really recommend this place.* ✓
- *In my opinion, I think …* ✗: choose one: *In my opinion, …* or *I think …*

id.text:
**Jebakan saat memberi rekomendasi:**
- *I recommend you to visit the night market.* ✗ → *I'd recommend **visiting** the night market.* / *I'd recommend **the night market**.* / *You **should visit** the night market.* ✓
- *It's worth **to visit**.* ✗ → *It's worth **visiting**.* ✓ (worth + -ing)
- *This place is very recommended.* ✗ (dari *sangat direkomendasikan*) → *I'd really recommend this place.* ✓
- *In my opinion, I think …* ✗: pilih salah satu: *In my opinion, …* atau *I think …*

options: It's worth to book a room early.
I recommend you to book a room early.
I'd recommend booking a room early.
blocks.explain: recommend + -ing: I'd recommend booking. 'It's worth to book' needs -ing (It's worth booking), and 'recommend you to' is a common mistake.

id.explain: recommend + -ing: I'd recommend booking. 'It's worth to book' harus memakai -ing (It's worth booking), dan 'recommend you to' adalah kesalahan yang umum.

material.title: Before you post it: a checklist

blocks.text:
Before you post or send your story or review, read it once more and check:
- **Title** and a **first line** that hooks the reader (no long greeting).
- **Paragraphs**: one main idea each, with a topic sentence first. A story: scene → events → ending. A review: opening → the good → the bad → opinion and recommendation.
- **Verbs**: in a story, every verb is in a past form (*went, saw, had left*); in a review, the present is fine for what the place is like (*The coffee is good*).
- **Sentences**: no 'and … and … and …' chains; one linker per sentence.
- **Length**: about 100 words (80–120).
- **The ending**: a feeling (story) or a recommendation (review).

id.text:
Sebelum kamu mengunggah atau mengirim cerita atau review-mu, baca sekali lagi dan periksa:
- **Judul** dan **kalimat pertama** yang mengait pembaca (tanpa salam panjang).
- **Paragraf**: masing-masing satu ide pokok, dengan topic sentence di awal. Cerita: latar → kejadian → akhir. Review: pembuka → sisi baik → sisi buruk → pendapat dan rekomendasi.
- **Kata kerja**: dalam cerita, setiap kata kerja memakai bentuk lampau (*went, saw, had left*); dalam review, present tense tidak apa-apa untuk menggambarkan tempatnya (*The coffee is good*).
- **Kalimat**: tanpa rantai 'and … and … and …'; satu linker per kalimat.
- **Panjang**: sekitar 100 kata (80–120).
- **Penutup**: perasaan (cerita) atau rekomendasi (review).

blocks.text: Write first, check later. When you write, don't stop at every word to translate. When you finish, read it out loud: if you need to breathe in the middle of a sentence, the sentence is probably too long.

id.text: Tulis dulu, periksa belakangan. Saat menulis, jangan berhenti di setiap kata untuk menerjemahkan. Setelah selesai, bacalah dengan suara keras: kalau kamu perlu menarik napas di tengah kalimat, kalimatnya mungkin terlalu panjang.

suggestedQuestions: How can I write a good first line for my story?
What is a topic sentence, and where do I put it?
How do I make my long sentences shorter?
What's the difference between 'I'd recommend' and 'It's worth'?

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Kamu sudah bisa bercerita secara lisan. Sekarang kamu akan menulis cerita: sekitar 100 kata dengan judul, kalimat pertama yang kuat dan paragraf yang jelas, lalu artikel atau review pendek yang berisi pendapat dan rekomendasimu. Apa itu topic sentence, dan di mana aku menaruhnya?
Bagaimana cara membuat kalimatku yang panjang jadi lebih pendek?

assessment.wsa-1: Lengkapi ceritanya dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'wait': It was a hot Saturday afternoon in Surabaya. Hundreds of football fans ___ outside the stadium when the gates suddenly opened.
assessment.wsa-2: Lengkapi dengan although, however atau because of: It was Saturday night at a popular seafood restaurant in Makassar. ___ we arrived early, all the tables were full, so we ate at a small warung next door.
assessment.wsa-3: Tiga kalimat ini membentuk satu paragraf artikel. Mana yang merupakan topic sentence? Tulis A, B atau C. A: On Jalan Sudirman, there is now a special lane for bikes. B: More and more office workers in Jakarta are cycling to work. C: Some offices also have showers and bike parking for their staff.
assessment.wsa-4: Baca paragrafnya. Ada satu kalimat yang tidak cocok, karena tidak mendukung topic sentence. Tulis nomornya. '(1) Bandung is a great place for a weekend trip from Jakarta. (2) It isn't far: you can get there by train or by car. (3) The weather is cooler, and there are lots of cafés and parks. (4) My cousin is studying medicine in Surabaya. (5) You can also buy cheap clothes at the factory outlets.'
assessment.wsa-5: Lengkapi kalimat terakhir sebuah review dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'see': The new photo exhibition at the National Museum is small, but the old photos of Jakarta are amazing, and tickets are only Rp15,000. It's really worth ___ .
assessment.wsa-6: Perbaiki kesalahan di kalimat terakhir review makanan ini, dalam bahasa Inggris: I recommend you to try the soto ayam.
